posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
Thank you Kaveh. Making these freely available is a wonderful gesture. Perhaps people too impatient to sit through interminable video clips will be inspired to check out the inconspicuous "order proceedings" link near the top to get the beautifully produced full-color printed proceeding with a very pretty embossed hologram on the cover, too! 

Since there is no obvious copyright notice listed, what is your policy regarding non-commercial mirroring of these clips to reduce your server load and bandwidth costs and improve service to some locales? Would this be welcome or discouraged? I have no means to do this, but if you thought it would be helpful, maybe someone would volunteer. Of course, given the small size of the potential audience, server loading could be a non-problem.

posts.author: Kaveh
posts.content_md:
Yes, I planted the "order proceedings" link in the hope of shifting some of these which cost a considerable sum to print!

I am happy with any mirroring I think, although I haven't given it much thought. Authors have signed copyright over to enable us to distribute these. My only request would be that if a paper is mirrored elsewhere, then users should be able to come to the main page to see other recordings. 

Any suggestions welcome.

posts.content_md:
> **Colin Kaminski:** OK, I tried that and I only got the first video. I have the settings to download all and to check manually. I clicked refresh and only got one video.

That's normal behaviour. It assumes you are listening or watching a regular podcast, e.g. a weekly episode. So it only downloads what it thinks is the most recent "show". So you will have to click on each episode to download. 

In the settings it is usual to have older episodes deleted. In this case you don't want that, so best to select the "isdh 2006" folder, right click and choose "Do not auto-delete".

> **Colin Kaminski:** But, there is only one Ipod link. Do I try the quicktime button or the flash button to get a Ipod cast of Jeff's lecture?

This is how it is on the Mac, and I think the same on Windows:

You click on the iTunes (purple) button. It should open up iTunes and subscribe to the feed. If that doesn't work, click the RSS link, then copy the "...rss.xml" url. Go to iTunes, choose "Advanced > Subscribe to PodCast..." and paste this text in. That should subscribe. 

Then in iTunes you should see a list of all the 50 or so talks, and it might download the top one. You can then choose which other ones to download. iTunes only works on the QuickTime version.

posts.content_md: Some AV applications are a pain in Windows. When you install them, by default the take all know movie extensions an associate them with their application. You can change this by opening Windows Explorer and then opening the Foler Options and go to the file types tab. Find the file type extension of the movie you are having problems with and make sure it is set to the correct application. If it is not, change it to the correct application.

posts.author: Kaveh
posts.content_md:
> **Sergio:** Look at these photos!http://www.diamondimages.com/holography ... /index.htm

The impromptu party at in Mark's room was memorable. (See page 4 of the photos.) 

When he invited *everyone* to his hotel room after the holography show, I thought he must have drunk a bit too much. He kept explaining how big his room was, and I tried to convince him he couldn't fit a whole conference delegation in it. But it turned out the rooms had run out and he had been allocated a two bedroom apartment with a huge area. I think we were all there, and magically various bottles and food appeared. There was a real sense of community, and just a happy, happy time. Thanks for the memory, Mark.
